turns.text:
I’ll check the buildability model and its required inputs, including layer height and the time between successive layers.
**The model classifies your wall as non-printable under the assumed printing schedule, with plastic collapse governing.** This is a screening result, not an experimentally established failure height.

Assumptions: **15 mm layer height, 35.53 mm filament width, 25 s layer cycle with no dwell**, fresh density **2,100 kg/m³**, load safety factor **1.5**, and a free-standing straight wall. Admixture percentages were interpreted as product mass relative to binder. Open time was unspecified.

| Physical check | Result |
|---|---|
| Target build | 27 layers; 11.25 min |
| Plastic collapse with structuration | Expected around layer 4, approximately 59 mm, before applying the safety factor |
| Free-wall buckling | Expected around layer 6, assuming elastic modulus/static yield stress = 25 |
| Open time | Cannot be checked without a measured value |

The rheology predictions are very uncertain: static yield stress **645 [28, 6,568] Pa** and structuration rate **0.586 [0.024, 14.518] Pa/s**, expressed as q50 [q10, q90]. Structuration is a **weak model: use it only as order-of-magnitude guidance**. Neither prediction exceeds the reported training ranges.

Published analogues provide firmer experimental context: [MK10 and MK5](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2022.128808), printed using a **30 mm nozzle and 15 mm layers**, collapsed in stack-to-failure tests at **339 and 311 mm**, respectively. These were hollow cylinders with different mixes, so they do not validate your straight wall.

To improve feasibility:

- **Increase material resistance:** at the current schedule, the calculator requires initial static yield stress of approximately **6,830 Pa**, holding structuration fixed, **or** structuration of **9.75 Pa/s**, holding initial yield stress fixed. These are alternative calculated requirements.
- **Slow the build:** the calculated minimum cycle is approximately **416 s**. A usable cycle-time window remains unconfirmed because open time is unknown, and buckling still needs checking.
- **Change geometry or formulation:** use thinner layers, widen or brace the wall, or trial an accelerator/VMA adjustment or lower w/b while checking extrusion.

Measure post-extrusion static yield stress, structuration and open time, then reassess with your actual layer dimensions. The final mix needs experimental verification.
